summary.text: An 11-year-old female with cystic fibrosis, confirmed by sweat chloride above 60 mmol/L and homozygosity for the ΔF508 mutation, presented at birth with meconium ileus requiring surgery. Childhood brought Pseudomonal and Staphylococcal chest infections and relapsing allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis treated with antibiotics, mucoactives, corticosteroids, antifungals and physiotherapy, then impaired glucose tolerance at age 9 and CF-related diabetes requiring insulin at 10 years.

Her BMI fell from the 64th to the 5th percentile in 10 months and growth did not respond to conservative dietary changes, including twice daily Enshake drinks. A PEG tube was inserted under general anesthetic two days after the second exercise test, and overnight supplemental feeding with 500 mL of Fresubin HP Energy was then introduced. During the 15-month period she was unstable and had 22 days of intravenous antibiotics.

Spirometry and exercise testing at four time points showed BMI percentile rising from 6.3 before the procedure to 38.1 at one year and weight from 33.3 to 42.5 kg, while FEV1 percent predicted fell from 77.1 to 59.9, weight-relative VO2max fell from 32.6 to 27.3 mL per kg per minute and VE/VO2 rose from 51.17 to 55.00. Absolute VO2max remained stable and lung function fluctuated with an overall declining trend.
